Reader's dictionary

How to Read This Ledger

The report uses technical shorthand. This page defines what each recurring term means in this experiment.

“Hidden” means internal—not secret.

A hidden-state method leaves the user-visible prompt unchanged. While the model generates its answer, we alter an internal residual activation at one registered layer. By contrast, the explicit-prompt control visibly asks the model to use emoji.

Same visible prompt“How should I plan a trip?”
→
Internal layer stateactivation vector h
→
Hidden interventionh′ = h + α||h||d̂
→
Generated answermeasure emoji + quality

Residual state / layer

The model's internal numerical representation at one depth: Qwen layer 20 or Gemma layer 32. It is not text and is different for every model.

Direction / vector

A same-size arrow in that internal space representing the change we want to add. CAA and NLA construct this arrow differently.

Alpha (α) / dose

How strongly the unit direction is added. Larger alpha means a stronger internal push—and usually more risk of distorted output.

NLA

Natural Language Autoencoder. AV turns an activation into readable text; AR reconstructs an activation from text. We edited the text, reconstructed both versions, and subtracted them.

CAA

Contrastive Activation Addition. Average many internal differences between matched emoji-positive and emoji-negative examples, then inject that mean direction.

Control

A comparison condition, not another claim. Baseline: no steering. Random: arbitrary internal push. Explicit: visible instruction asking for emoji.

Calibration / frozen alpha

Try doses on six separate prompts, reject unsafe doses, then lock one dose. “Frozen” means it could not be changed after seeing held-out results.

Held-out / paired

Held-out: 40 prompts excluded from dose choice. Paired: compare the same prompt and generation seed with versus without steering.

Primary and secondary tracks

The 30 ordinary prompts are primary. The 10 formal/technical prompts test transfer or intrusion and are analyzed separately—never pooled.

Emoji presence

The primary outcome is binary: did the response contain at least one Unicode emoji cluster? ASCII emoticons and the total emoji count are secondary.

pp, effect, and 95% CI

pp means percentage points: 0% to 15.8% is +15.8 pp. The 95% interval shows prompt-level uncertainty around that paired effect.

Deterministic safety / failure

Frozen automatic checks for shortening, repetition, corrupted characters, or emoji flooding. Failure means a threshold was crossed—not necessarily human-rated nonsense. “Supported†” still awaits blinded relevance/fluency ratings.

Reading rule: hidden methods change an internal activation; explicit prompting changes the text the user can see.25 August 2026

Frozen held-out comparison · Qwen L20 + Gemma L32

The Cross-Model Emoji Steering Ledger

A unified record of three matched hidden-state constructions, two independently calibrated models, and one result that clearly replicated.

Did hidden-state steering make both models use emoji? Yes.

The NLA direction built by appending one smile glyph to the model's verbalized state increased held-out emoji presence in Qwen and Gemma. CAA and the longer phrase direction were positive only in Gemma at their frozen safe doses.

+15.8 ppQwen NLA-glyph effect on ordinary prompts; 95% CI 7.5 to 25.8
+28.3 ppGemma NLA-glyph effect on ordinary prompts; 95% CI 18.3 to 39.2
6,240archived held-out rows across both runs; paired and repeated cells, not independent samples
Headline: the minimal NLA glyph construction replicated; method efficacy was still model-dependent.25 August 2026

Matched design

What was held constant—and what was rebuilt

The user-visible hidden-arm prompts were identical. The vectors were not: every direction was constructed fresh inside the target model's registered residual space.

Frozen inputs30 ordinary + 10 formal
→
Build per modelQwen L20 or Gemma L32
→
Injecth + α||h||d̂
→
Paired scoresame prompt + seed
1CAA

Average 300 activation contrasts

d = mean(h_positive_answer − h_negative_answer)

Balanced A/B answer letters from 300 frozen AxBench-derived text inputs; oriented toward the emoji-positive requirement.

2NLA phrase

Edit one verbalized state

AR(z + “The response should include Unicode emojis and emoticons.”) − AR(z)

No averaging. AV produces the readable state; AR reconstructs original and edited text into residual vectors.

3NLA glyph

Append one smile glyph

AR(z + “😊”) − AR(z)

The smallest frozen semantic edit. This was the only construction with a clear positive result in both models.

Matched administration. Each unit direction used the same decode-time all-position hook, temperature 0.7, 192-token ceiling, 40 prompts, and four prompt-specific paired seeds.
Independently calibrated. Qwen and Gemma used different alpha ladders and each method selected its own safe dose before held-out evaluation.
No vector transport. Qwen d=3,584 vectors never entered Gemma d=3,840 space. This is a shared-text protocol, not a shared-vector test.
ComponentFrozen choice
Prompt source40 outcome-blind AxBench Concept500 input rows; expected outputs and concept labels were not used to score steering
Primary track30 ordinary, emoji-optional prompts × 4 generations = 120 paired cells/model
Secondary track10 formal/technical prompts × 4 generations = 40 paired cells/model; never pooled with primary
ControlsUnsteered baseline, 3 isotropic random directions, and a visible explicit-prompt upper bound
This is an AxBench-derived prompt study, not an official AxBench benchmark score.25 August 2026

Controls and quality

The effect sits between a silent baseline and an explicit ceiling

Baseline responses contained no Unicode emoji. Explicitly requesting emoji produced them in every response, showing a much stronger visible-prompt upper bound.

Qwen glyph: 96.9% safe; conservative recoding still gives +11.7 pp.
Gemma glyph: 98.8% safe; conservative recoding still gives +26.7 pp.
Not yet established: deterministic coherence is not the same as instruction relevance or fluency. Qwen's 240-row and Gemma's 200-row blinded quality sheets remain unrated.
Unsafe outputs remain in the archive; the sensitivity analysis does not delete or conceal them.25 August 2026

J-space boundary

Why the direct J-lens arm is not in the matched result

The Qwen archive includes one direct J-lens token atom. The Gemma run intentionally omitted behavioral J-lens steering, so it cannot be presented as a two-model comparison.

The main comparison is CAA versus two NLA edit constructions.

Qwen's direct “ emoji” atom is preserved exactly as completed, but it produced 0.0 pp at its safe alpha 0.10 and remains exploratory. No completed Qwen data were deleted.

What Qwen actually ran

Direct J-atom injection

d = Jᵀ(norm-scale × unembedding[token])

The atom was stable across split WikiText lens halves (cosine 0.938) but behaviorally null at the safe dose.

What this was not

Not the earlier k=25 split

This new direct atom did not approximate an NLA parent with 25 atoms, did not inject a parent-minus-approximation remainder, and did not move a live activation component between models.

Main matched reportCAA + NLA phrase + NLA glyph
≠
Qwen exploratory armone direct J-lens token atom
≠
Earlier J-derived workk=25 approximation + remainder
≠
Future matched J testwould require a frozen two-model protocol
Interpretation: split-half stability says the fitted token direction was reproducible under that corpus split. It does not imply behavioral sufficiency. The direct atom's null result does not invalidate J-space generally.
Gemma J-lens construction artifacts may exist for diagnostics; no Gemma J-lens behavioral arm was generated here.25 August 2026

Claims, limits, and provenance

What the combined experiment proves—and what it does not

The strongest defensible conclusion is narrower than “emoji steering always works,” but stronger than a one-model anecdote.

Supported nowAt calibrated safe doses, the minimal NLA glyph construction increased Unicode-emoji presence on held-out ordinary prompts in both Qwen and Gemma.
Supported in Gemma onlyThis CAA construction and the longer NLA phrase construction cleared the frozen within-Gemma statistical and deterministic gates.
Not supportedA model-independent ranking of CAA versus NLA; equal-alpha superiority; transport of a residual vector across models; uniform transfer to formal/technical prompts.
Still pendingBlinded instruction-relevance and fluency ratings. Until completed, do not state that instruction quality was fully preserved.
Exploratory onlyQwen's direct J-lens atom null and all prompt-type heterogeneity observations.
40same frozen held-out prompts per model: 30 primary ordinary + 10 secondary formal
4paired generations per prompt, with prompt-specific seeds reused across arms
3 + 3matched treatment constructions plus three independent random-direction controls
